summary.text: Coastal morphodynamics studies how coastal landforms interact with physical processes such as waves, tides, currents, wind, moving sediment and severe weather.
Moving water responds at once when a beach's shape changes, but the beach can only reshape by moving sediment, which takes time, so its response lags behind.
Because the waves and other forces acting on a beach change regularly, the beach never reaches equilibrium.

items.prompt: A big storm with steep waves hits a steep beach of coarse sand. How does the beach's profile tend to change?

options.label: It gets even steeper as sand piles up
It stays the same, as coarse sand never moves
It flattens as sand moves out offshore
It turns into a rocky cliff within days

items.explain: Storms tend to flatten reflective beaches by moving sediment offshore under steeper waves, giving a more dissipative profile.

items.prompt: Why can a beach of coarse sand keep a steep slope while waves keep running up and down it?

options.label: Coarse grains are too heavy for any wave to lift
Water drains into the gaps, weakening the backwash
Coarse sand sticks together when it gets wet
Waves never reach the steep part of the beach

items.explain: Coarse sediment lets water percolate in during the swash, which weakens the backwash so material is left in the swash zone.

items.prompt: Wave conditions change sharply overnight, yet the beach's shape takes much longer to catch up. Why the delay?

options.label: Reshaping it means moving sediment, which takes time
Waves cannot affect a beach until the tide turns
The beach first has to dry out in the sun
Sand only moves during the calm summer months

items.explain: Water responds instantly, but changing the landform requires sediment to be redistributed, which takes a finite time, so the shape lags behind the forcing.

items.prompt: A researcher plans to measure a beach once it finally settles into a fixed, stable shape. Why will that moment never come?

options.label: Sand slowly dissolves away in seawater
Beaches are always sinking into the seabed
Instruments disturb the sand they measure
The forces acting on it keep changing

items.explain: The boundary conditions of wave and current forcing change regularly, so the beach never attains equilibrium.

items.prompt: You reach a wide, flat beach of fine sand where waves start breaking far out and roll in gently across a broad surf zone. What type of beach is this?

options.label: A reflective beach
A dissipative beach
A surging beach
A pebble beach

items.explain: Dissipative beaches are flat with fine sand, and their waves break far from the shore and lose force gradually across wide surf zones.

items.prompt: A town wants to know how a new sea wall might alter its shoreline in coming years. How can this field of study help?

options.label: It can stop all waves from reaching the coast
It can only describe how the coast looked in the past
It can guarantee the beach will never erode again
Its models can anticipate changes from human activity

items.explain: The field uses observations and models to anticipate coastal change, and its conclusions give insight into how human activity affects coastal systems.
